clue.text: Conservative legislation reintroduced to bring financial recoupment?

parts.note: legislation is law
something reintroduced is brought back

explanation.surface: A Tory law brought back to recover money from people.
explanation.definitionFit: A recovery of money already paid out, such as by a government, is called this; the question mark admits the cryptic stretch.

clue.text: Cold rebel touchy and irritable

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a hippy is a counterculture rebel

explanation.surface: A rebel with a chill is prickly and bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: having a chip on one's shoulder, so touchy and irritable.

clue.text: Seem to be a listener keeping very quiet

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the quiet letters go within

parts.note: taken as written
an ear is what listens
PP, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet

explanation.surface: Seeming to be someone listening while staying very quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to seem or look as if.

clue.text: Obtains new defence

indicators.note: new says the letters of obtains are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone acquires a new defensive structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a bastion is a fortified stronghold, a defence.

clue.text: Result of trick on train

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
a train of events is a sequence

explanation.surface: The outcome of a scam carried out on a railway train.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an outcome or effect.

clue.text: Famous US science teacher's optical instruments

definitions.meaning: John Thomas ... was the Tennessee teacher tried in 1925 for teaching evolution; the 's here reads as 'is'
microscopes, telescopes and the like are often called by this short plural

explanation.surface: A celebrated American science teacher's telescopes and microscopes.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the teacher in the 1925 'Monkey Trial' is also the short plural for viewing instruments.

clue.text: Officer, one taking line south of mountain pass

indicators.note: in a down entry, south of puts the following pieces below the pass

parts.note: a col is a pass between mountain peaks
taken as written

explanation.surface: An officer crossing a mountain pass to the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a colonel is a senior army officer.

clue.text: Completely heartless paper with monstrous female given advancement

indicators.note: completely heartless says all the middle of the word is removed, keeping only its ends

parts.note: an ogress is a female monster

explanation.surface: A heartless newspaper with a monster of a woman gets promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Completely heartless' strips APE from PAPER, leaving PR.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: progress is forward movement, advancement.

clue.text: Dotty is sedate, showing reserve

indicators.note: dotty means crazy, so the letters of is sedate are scrambled

explanation.surface: A dotty person is calm, showing restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to set aside is to keep back for later, to reserve.

clue.text: This person's posturing as impressive

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself: this person is = I am, contracted to I'M
posturing is striking poses, posing

explanation.surface: Someone striking attitudes in order to look impressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something grand and impressive in appearance is said to be stately or commanding.

clue.text: Probing hospital, MO started pretty well

indicators.note: a probe goes into something, so the answer sits inside these clue words

explanation.surface: A doctor's probe in hospital has very nearly started.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across hospitAL MOSTarted; 'MO' is no abbreviation to use here.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: pretty well means nearly or all but.

clue.text: Management of image by company with a policy to be sweet

parts.note: public relations, PR, is the managing of a firm's image
taken as written
a policy is a line, as in a party line

explanation.surface: A firm's spin doctors adopt a policy of being nice.
explanation.definitionFit: A praline is a confection of nuts and caramelised sugar, so a sweet.

clue.text: Fellow, sure clumsy, gets covered in muck

definitions.note: verb sense: the answer means covers (land) in muck, the clue's 'gets covered' read loosely

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: clumsy says the letters of sure are handled awkwardly and rearranged

explanation.surface: A clumsy man ends up covered in dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread dung over fields is to fertilise them, covering them in muck.

clue.text: Businesses stalled here?

parts.note: stalled suggests halted, but traders set up in market stalls

explanation.definitionFit: A market square is where traders run their businesses from stalls.

clue.text: Crazy leader is nut to be made ineffective

indicators.note: crazy says the letters of leader is nut are scrambled

explanation.surface: A mad leader who is a nutcase must be neutralised.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something rendered harmless or cancelled out has been made ineffective.

clue.text: Disorder aboard ship making trips

indicators.note: aboard puts the disorder inside the ship

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the usual abbreviation for a ship
a tumble is a state of disorder, as hair in a tumble

explanation.surface: Chaos on board ship sends people tripping.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: one who trips over something stumbles.

clue.text: Man perhaps overcome by beautiful sort of design

indicators.note: in a down entry, overcome by puts the island beneath the word for beautiful

parts.note: fair means beautiful
the Isle of Man is an example of an isle

explanation.surface: A man perhaps overwhelmed by a lovely type of pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person, but it is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea. The knitting pattern is named after an island in Shetland.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a traditional multicoloured knitwear pattern from the Shetland island.

clue.text: Imbibers who go to pot?

parts.note: going to pot sounds like decline, but these drinkers literally head for the teapot

explanation.definitionFit: People who drink a brew poured from a pot are tippling, but on the cup that cheers.

clue.text: One taking practical approach is on a roll

parts.note: on in the sense of about, concerning, is RE
a roll is a list of names; the a is taken as written
a roll is a list of names; the a is taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sensible is having a run of success.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pragmatic person who faces facts as they are.

clue.text: Gun beginning to scare owl?

indicators.note: beginning to says take the first letter of the next word

parts.note: an owl hoots, so it is a hooter, the query admitting the whimsy

explanation.surface: A gun going off starts to frighten an owl.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a shooter is a gun.

clue.text: Spell out letters at end of crossword clue, all right?

indicators.note: the letters at the end of each of the two words are taken

parts.note: all right means fine

explanation.surface: Spell out the letters at the end of a crossword clue, okay?
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to explain the meaning of, to spell out.

clue.text: Sanction at the moment that gets transmitted

parts.note: as can mean while or at the moment that
something transmitted has been sent

explanation.surface: Approval given right when a message is sent.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: agreement or approval, a sanction.

clue.text: Wreck entrance in seaside resort

parts.note: to wreck is to mar
an entrance is a gate

explanation.surface: Damaging an entry in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: MARGATE is a seaside resort on the Kent coast in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Kent town is a classic British holiday destination by the sea.

clue.text: Claim made by little old female in crowd

indicators.note: in places the old woman inside the crowd

parts.note: a press is a crowd or throng
O is the short form of old

explanation.surface: A statement made by a small elderly woman in a throng.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to claim or declare openly.

clue.text: Girl, one in spectacles putting off outsiders

indicators.note: the outer letters are shed from what is built

parts.note: spectacles are glasses
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A girl wearing glasses takes off strangers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I into GLASSES to give GLASSIES; 'putting off outsiders' removes G and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a lass, a young girl, especially in Scotland and northern England.

clue.text: Not wholly engaged at work?

parts.note: an employee not engaged all week works a fraction of the hours

explanation.definitionFit: Someone employed for only some of the working week is not engaged wholly.

clue.text: Becomes aware of meaning when listening

indicators.note: listening says the word for meaning is heard rather than read

parts.note: meaning is sense

explanation.surface: Someone picks up on the meaning while listening.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to detect or perceive something, as an animal does a smell.

clue.text: Bishop most strange and least likely to be sober?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
most strange is eeriest

explanation.surface: A very odd bishop is the one most likely to be drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Most full of ale, so most tipsy and least likely to be sober.
